decisions.choice: Moses went and spoke (the traditional Hebrew text)
alternatives: Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel (a Dead Sea Scroll and the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text reads "Moses went and spoke these words". One of the Dead Sea Scrolls of Deuteronomy and the ancient Greek translation read instead "Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel". In Hebrew the two readings differ only in the order of a few letters. The other reading would make this verse close the speech of chapters 29-30, in the way 31:24 and 32:45 mark an ending. We follow the traditional Hebrew text, which makes the verse introduce the words that follow. This account of the evidence is from general knowledge and must be checked against the textual sources before review.

decisions.choice: went and spoke: set about speaking; these words point ahead to verses 2-6
decisions.reason: The verb "went" often begins a new action without a journey: Moses turns to a new task. In the traditional text "these words" are the words that follow, Moses' farewell charge to the people in verses 2-6.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "All Israel" means the whole people. Readable says so in plain words.

decisions.choice: the narrator's frame in chapter 31 in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("alla", "dit", "écrivit") and the passé composé at Readable ("est allé", "a écrit"); Moses' and God's speeches use the ordinary spoken tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in 1:1-5: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the one young readers use; Readable keeps to it.

decisions.choice: go out and come in: lead the people in war and in their daily life
decisions.reason: The pair of verbs describes a leader's whole work, going out at the head of the people and bringing them back (Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11). Moses is not saying that his body has failed, since 34:7 says his strength had not left him. He is saying that his time to lead is over, because God has said he will not cross.

decisions.choice: You shall not cross this Jordan: God's earlier word to Moses
decisions.reason: God refused to let Moses enter the land because of what happened at Meribah (Numbers 20:12), and refused again when Moses pleaded with him (3:23-27; 1:37).

decisions.choice: a son of 120 years: 120 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the "son" of so many years.

decisions.choice: go out and come in before you; Readable "lead you"
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew pair and adds "before you" to show it is about leading the people. Readable says what the pair means.

source.text: יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ ה֣וּא׀עֹבֵ֣ר לְפָנֶ֗יךָ הֽוּא־יַשְׁמִ֞יד אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֛לֶּה מִלְּפָנֶ֖יךָ וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֑ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ ה֚וּא עֹבֵ֣ר לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh your God, he [is] crossing before you; he will destroy the nations the these from before you, and you will dispossess them; Joshua, he [is] crossing before you, just as spoke Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one crossing over before you; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua, he [is] the one crossing over before you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is the one who will cross over before you. He will wipe out these nations in your path, and you will drive them out. Joshua too will cross over at your head, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will go across ahead of you. He will destroy these nations as you advance, and you will drive them out. Joshua will also go ahead of you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [es] el que pasa delante de ti; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} destruirá estas naciones de delante de ti, y tú las desposeerás. Josué, él [es] el que pasa delante de ti, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo cruzará delante de ti. Él aniquilará a estas naciones a tu paso, y tú las expulsarás. También Josué cruzará al frente de ti, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dicho.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios irá delante de ti al otro lado. Él destruirá a estas naciones a medida que avances, y tú las echarás. Josué también irá delante de ti, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo prometió.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui passe devant toi ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui détruira ces nations de devant toi, et tu les déposséderas. Josué, c’est lui qui passe devant toi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a dit.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu passera {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} devant toi. Il anéantira ces nations sur ton passage, et tu les chasseras. Josué aussi passera à ta tête, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a dit.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va traverser devant toi. Il détruira ces nations à mesure que tu avanceras, et tu les chasseras. Josué aussi ira devant toi, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a promis.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ndiye] anayevuka mbele yako; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atayaangamiza mataifa haya mbele yako, nawe utawarithi. Yoshua, yeye [ndiye] anayevuka mbele yako, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye atakayevuka mbele yako. Atayaangamiza mataifa haya mbele yako, nawe utawafukuza. Yoshua naye atavuka akikuongoza, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyosema.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atatangulia mbele yako kuvuka. Atayaangamiza mataifa haya unaposonga mbele, nawe utawafukuza. Yoshua pia atakutangulia, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoahidi.

decisions.choice: he ... he: God himself goes first, and Joshua goes with the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets an emphatic "he" before God's crossing and another before Joshua's. God is the one who really goes ahead and wins the battles; Joshua leads the people under him. Moses' absence will not leave Israel without a leader.

decisions.choice: dispossess them: drive the nations out and take over what they held
decisions.reason: With nations as its object this verb means to drive them out and take their place (as in 9:1; 11:23). It is the same verb used for Israel taking possession of the land.

decisions.choice: as the LORD has spoken: God's appointment of Joshua
decisions.reason: God told Moses to appoint Joshua as his successor (Numbers 27:18-23) and to encourage him because he would lead the people across (1:38; 3:28).

decisions.choice: himself; "Joshua too" / "Joshua will also"
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the stress of the Hebrew "he" with "himself". "Too" and "also" show that Joshua goes ahead as well, under God.

source.text: וְעָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה לְסִיח֥וֹן וּלְע֛וֹג מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י וּלְאַרְצָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁמִ֖יד אֹתָֽם׃

en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will destroy them, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and their land.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur fera comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait à Sihon et à Og, les rois des Amoréens, et à leur pays, lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a détruits.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les traitera comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a traité Sihon et Og, les rois amoréens, ainsi que leur pays, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a détruits.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les détruira, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a détruit Sihon et Og, les rois des Amoréens, et leur pays.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawatendea kama alivyowatendea Sihoni na Ogu, wafalme wa Waamori, na nchi yao, alipowaangamiza.

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the two kings defeated east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan and took their land (2:26-3:11; Numbers 21:21-35). Those victories are proof of what God will do west of the river (3:21).

decisions.choice: whom he destroyed: the kings, with their land
decisions.reason: The closing clause looks back to the kings and their land together: God destroyed them and their rule.

source.text: וּנְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will give them Yahweh before you, and you will do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give them over before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hand them over to you, and you must deal with them exactly as I have commanded you.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let you defeat them. Then you must do to them everything I have commanded you.

es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dará la victoria sobre ellos. Entonces {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} que hacer con ellos todo lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} he mandado.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les livrera devant vous, et vous leur ferez selon tout le commandement que je vous ai commandé.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous les livrera, et vous devrez les traiter exactement comme je vous l’ai ordonné.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous donnera la victoire sur eux. Alors vous devrez leur faire tout ce que je vous ai ordonné.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawatoa mbele yenu, nanyi mtawatendea sawasawa na amri yote niliyowaamuru.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawatia mikononi mwenu, nanyi mtawatendea kikamilifu kama nilivyowaagiza.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawawezesha kuwashinda. Kisha lazima mwatendee kila kitu nilichowaamuru.

decisions.choice: give them before you: put them in your power
decisions.reason: To "give" an enemy "before" someone is to let that person defeat them (2:33; 7:2, 23).

decisions.choice: all the commandment I have commanded you: the orders about the nations of the land
decisions.reason: "Commandment" is singular, the whole charge Moses has given. Here it points to the orders for dealing with the nations of the land: to make no covenant with them, to destroy their altars and to devote them to destruction (7:1-5; 20:16-18).

decisions.choice: exactly as / everything I have commanded
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "according to all the commandment". Balanced and Readable fold the singular noun into the verb, which says the same thing.

records.literal_gloss: Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not tremble from before them, for Yahweh your God, he [is] the [one] going with you; not he will let you drop, and not he will forsake you.

en.L: Be strong and be courageous; do not fear and do not tremble before them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one who goes with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forsake you."
en.B: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid of them or tremble before them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one who goes with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not abandon you."
en.R: Be strong and brave! Do not be afraid of them or let them frighten you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going with you. He will not let go of you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not leave you on your own."

es.B: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valientes. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de ellos ni {{plural_you:tiemblen|tembléis}} ante ellos, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios es quien va contigo. No te soltará ni te abandonará».
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valientes! No {{plural_you:les tengan|les tengáis}} miedo ni {{plural_you:se dejen|os dejéis}} asustar por ellos. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} va con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. fr.L: Soyez forts et soyez courageux ; ne craignez pas et ne tremblez pas devant eux, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui marche avec toi. Il ne te lâchera pas et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’abandonnera pas. »
fr.B: Soyez forts et courageux. N’ayez pas peur d’eux et ne tremblez pas devant eux, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu est celui qui marche avec toi. Il ne te lâchera pas et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’abandonnera pas. »
fr.R: Soyez forts et courageux ! N’ayez pas peur d’eux, ne vous laissez pas effrayer par eux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu marche avec vous. Il ne vous lâchera pas, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne vous laissera pas seuls. »

sw.B: Iweni imara na hodari. Msiwaogope wala msitetemeke mbele yao, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako ndiye anayekwenda pamoja nawe. Hatakuachilia, wala hatakutupa."
sw.R: Iweni imara na jasiri! Msiwaogope, wala msiwaache wawatishe. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu anakwenda pamoja nanyi. Hatawaachilia, wala hatawaacha peke yenu."

decisions.choice: be strong and be bold: stand firm and have courage
decisions.reason: The two verbs together are the charge to hold firm and act bravely in the face of danger. Moses gives it here to the whole people, and then to Joshua (verses 7, 23; 3:28; Joshua 1:6-9).

decisions.choice: let you drop: let go of you, loosen his hold
decisions.reason: The first verb means to let something fall slack, to let go of it. The second means to leave behind or abandon. Together they promise that God will not loosen his grip on his people or leave them on their own (verse 8; Joshua 1:5).

decisions.choice: you: the people, plural and then singular
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, spoken to all the people. "Your God" and "with you" are singular, as Deuteronomy often speaks to Israel as one person.

decisions.choice: let you go / let go of you
decisions.reason: The English keeps the picture of loosening a hold, which the Hebrew verb has, instead of a more general word such as "fail".

decisions.choice: plural commands ("sean", "no teman") then singular "tu Dios", "contigo" at Literal and Balanced; Readable keeps the plural through the verse ("su Dios", "con ustedes")
decisions.reason: Spanish can show the Hebrew shift from all the people to Israel as one (see the meaning decision); Readable keeps one number so the verse is easy to follow.

decisions.choice: "Soyez forts" (vous) then "ton Dieu", "avec toi" (tu) at Literal and Balanced; Readable keeps "vous" through the verse
decisions.reason: French follows the Hebrew number, as elsewhere in Deuteronomy; Readable keeps one number so the verse is easy to follow.

decisions.reason: "imara" (firm) and "hodari" (bold) keep the two Hebrew verbs apart; "jasiri" is the plainer word for brave. The same pair is used for Joshua in verses 7 and 23.

en.L: And Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and be courageous, for you shall go with this people into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to their fathers to give to them, and you shall cause them to inherit it.
en.B: Then Moses summoned Joshua and, with all Israel looking on, said to him, "Be strong and courageous. You are the one who will go with this people into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance.
en.R: Then Moses called for Joshua. With all Israel watching, he said to him, "Be strong and brave. You will go with these people into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give their ancestors. You will give it to them as their own.

es.L: Y llamó Moisés a Josué y le dijo a la vista de todo Israel: «Sé fuerte y sé valiente, porque tú entrarás con este pueblo en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró a sus padres que les daría, y tú se la harás heredar.
es.B: Entonces Moisés convocó a Josué y, ante la mirada de todo Israel, le dijo: «Sé fuerte y valiente. Tú eres quien irá con este pueblo a la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró dar a sus antepasados, y tú se la repartirás como herencia.
es.R: Después Moisés llamó a Josué. Delante de todo Israel le dijo: «Sé fuerte y valiente. Tú irás con esta gente a la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} prometió con juramento dar a sus antepasados. Tú se la darás para que sea suya.

fr.L: Et Moïse appela Josué et lui dit sous les yeux de tout Israël : « Sois fort et sois courageux, car c’est toi qui iras avec ce peuple dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré à leurs pères de leur donner, et c’est toi qui le leur feras hériter.
fr.B: Puis Moïse convoqua Josué et, sous le regard de tout Israël, lui dit : « Sois fort et courageux. C’est toi qui entreras avec ce peuple dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré à leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} de leur donner, et c’est toi qui le leur partageras en héritage.
fr.R: Ensuite, Moïse a appelé Josué. Devant tout Israël, il lui a dit : « Sois fort et courageux. Tu vas aller avec ce peuple dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a promis par serment de donner à leurs {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. C’est toi qui le leur donneras, pour qu’il soit à eux.

sw.L: Musa akamwita Yoshua, akamwambia mbele ya macho ya Israeli wote, "Uwe imara, uwe hodari, kwa maana wewe utakwenda pamoja na watu hawa katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia baba zao kwamba atawapa, nawe utawarithisha.

sw.R: Kisha Musa alimwita Yoshua. Israeli wote wakiwa wanatazama, alimwambia, "Uwe imara na jasiri. Utakwenda pamoja na watu hawa katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliahidi kwa kiapo kuwapa mababu zao. Wewe utawapa nchi hiyo iwe yao.

decisions.choice: in the sight of all Israel: a public commissioning
decisions.reason: Moses hands over the leadership before the whole people, so that everyone knows who will lead them and that he has Moses' authority (Numbers 27:19-20).

decisions.choice: cause them to inherit it: lead them in and share out the land
decisions.reason: As in 1:38 and 3:28, the verb means to give others an inheritance. Joshua will bring the people into the land and divide it among the tribes (Joshua 14:1).

decisions.choice: you will go with this people (the traditional Hebrew text)
alternatives: you will bring this people (Samaritan Pentateuch, some ancient translations)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text reads "you will go with this people". The Samaritan Pentateuch and some ancient translations read "you will bring this people", with the same verb God uses in verse 23. The difference is one small change of vowels and a letter. We follow the traditional text. This account of the evidence is from general knowledge and must be checked against the textual sources before review.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathers", meaning forefathers. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", as in 1:8.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui marche devant toi ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sera avec toi. Il ne te lâchera pas et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne t’abandonnera pas. Ne crains pas et ne te laisse pas abattre. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ndiye] anayekwenda mbele yako; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atakuwa pamoja nawe. Hatakuachilia, wala hatakutupa. Usiogope wala usifadhaike."

decisions.choice: you: now Joshua alone
decisions.reason: Every "you" in this verse is singular and speaks to Joshua. He receives in person the promise Moses has just given to all the people in verse 6, almost word for word.

decisions.choice: be dismayed: be shattered, lose heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken or shattered, and of people to be terrified or lose all courage (1:21; Joshua 1:9).

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the stress of the Hebrew "he" with "himself", as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Readable adds "So" to show that the commands follow from the promise.

en.L: And Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to all the elders of Israel.
en.B: Then Moses put this law in writing. He handed it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who were the bearers of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to all of Israel's elders.
en.R: Moses wrote down this teaching. He gave it to the priests from the tribe of Levi, the men who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He also gave it to all the leaders of Israel.

fr.R: Moïse a écrit cet enseignement. Il l’a donné aux prêtres de la tribu de Lévi, les hommes qui portaient l’arche de l’alliance {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Il l’a aussi donné à tous les chefs d’Israël.

decisions.choice: this law: the whole of Moses' teaching in this book
decisions.reason: As in 1:5, "law" is instruction: the whole body of Moses' teaching, history and appeal as well as rules. Now it is set down in writing (verse 24; 17:18).

decisions.choice: the priests who carried the ark
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark (10:8), and in the crossing of the Jordan the priests carry it (Joshua 3:3). Giving the written law to the priests and the elders puts it in the care of both the religious and the civil leaders.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the Hebrew word Literal and Balanced render "law", as in 1:5.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable calls the elders "leaders", which says what they were: the senior men who led the tribes and towns.

decisions.choice: at the end of seven years: in the seventh year
decisions.reason: As in 15:1, "at the end of seven years" means in the last year of each seven, the year of release, not after it.

decisions.choice: the year of release: the seventh year, when debts were canceled
decisions.reason: Every seventh year Israelites were to release their fellow Israelites from debts (15:1-3). The same word is used of letting the land rest in the seventh year (Exodus 23:11).

decisions.choice: the festival of booths: the autumn harvest festival
decisions.reason: The festival was held for seven days after the harvest, at the place God would choose; the people lived in shelters made of branches to remember the wilderness journey (16:13-15; Leviticus 23:33-43). In the year of release the whole nation would be gathered there.

decisions.choice: the year when debts are canceled
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the year of release was.

decisions.choice: "el año de la remisión"
decisions.reason: "Remisión" is the word for cancelling a debt, which is what this year does (15:1-3); Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "l'année de la remise"
decisions.reason: "Remise" (de dette) names the cancelling of debts that marks this year (15:1-3); Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "mwaka wa maachilio"
decisions.reason: "Maachilio" (release, letting go) keeps the Hebrew name of the year; Readable says what it was, "mwaka ambao madeni husamehewa", as the English does.

decisions.choice: the place he will choose: the one place of worship
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy looks ahead to one place where God will put his name and where Israel will bring its offerings and keep its festivals (12:5; 16:16).

decisions.choice: to appear before the LORD
decisions.reason: The vowels of the traditional text read the verb as "to be seen", that is, to appear before the LORD, as in 16:16. The same consonants could be read "to see the face of the LORD". The sense is the same: the people come before God at his sanctuary.

decisions.choice: you shall read: singular
decisions.reason: "You" is singular. It may speak to Israel as one, or to the leader who will stand before the people. The reading was done by a leader in later times (Joshua 8:34-35; 2 Kings 23:2; Nehemiah 8:1-3).

decisions.choice: aloud ... so that they hear it
decisions.reason: "In their ears" means in their hearing. Balanced and Readable say the reading was aloud, for all to hear.

decisions.choice: stand before
decisions.reason: Readable says "stand before" for the less common "appear before".
